newsitem.title: JAPAN: Big Japanese realtor declared bankrupt.
newsitem.headline: Big Japanese realtor declared bankrupt.

text.p: A major realtor with debts of more than $6 billion has been declared bankrupt in the second-largest insolvency case in Japan since World War II, the semi-official Housing Loan Administration Corp. said Monday.

Sueno Kosan, based in Osaka in western Japan, was a major borrower from failed "jusen" mortgage firms. A court's declaration of its insolvency came after the Housing Loan Administration sought involuntary bankruptcy for the company and two of its units last month.
An official at the authority, set up to collect problem loans run up by the jusen firms this year, said Sueno's two units were also declared insolvent by the Osaka court.
Total debts of Sueno and its two units are about 970 billion yen ($8.73 billion).
In October, non-bank Nichiei Finance Co. Ltd went under with total debts of about one trillion yen ($9.0 billion), the biggest bankruptcy case in Japan.
Sueno Kosan, set up in February 1979, expanded its real estate business rapidly in the late 1980s "bubble" era of inflated stock and land prices.
But after the "bubble" burst in the early 1990s and a protracted real estate market slump ensued, its business deteriorated and it faced difficulty in raising funds.
